newsitem.title: UK: Mideast/Japan VLCC rates hit post-Gulf War high.
newsitem.headline: Mideast/Japan VLCC rates hit post-Gulf War high.

text.p: Chartering rates for very large crude carriers (VLCCs) reached new heights on Friday, exceeding W90 for the first time since the Gulf War, shipbrokers said.
Aframax 80,000 tonne vessels crossing northwest Europe jumped 15-20 worldscale points in the meantime to W135, brokers said.
Idemitsu's reported fixture of the 262,000 tonne Ambon to Japan at W90.75 underlined the strength of the market. "That is now the going rate," one broker said.
Dealers also said one U.S. major was seeking a 400,000 tonne vessel for a Mideast/Ain Sukhna voyage and only one or two offers were heard available - at W107.50.
"That offer was a little bit tongue in cheek but this is a sign that Mideast/Japan is going to get stronger," another broker said. "I think we are going to see over W100."
Strength in the Suezmax sector this week, partly caused by the reemergence of Iraqi oil onto world markets under a U.N. deal, is spilling over into other tanker markets.
Three fresh fixtures were seen for 80,000 tonne Aframax tankers crossing the UK/Cont region at W135, compared to brokers' assessments on Thursday at W115-W120.
"There is a lot of pressure on tonnage," a broker said. "There has been a bit of parcelling on to Suezmaxes but it has not been enough. Basically ships are in short supply."
Suezmax rates from West Africa to the U.S. Gulf built on the week's gains and were talked close to W97.50-W100 by the day's end.
And 260,000 tonners found themselves in better demand in West Africa, with rates to the U.S. Gulf rising by nearly five points to around W75.
"I can't see it going down," a broker said.
